+User decision 2026-10-23: make the keychain a parameter of `KeychainSecretStore`, and have the integration test create and use a temporary keychain.
+
+## Why
+CI on main has not passed since 2026-10-20 12:39. The only test failure: `IntegrationTests/.../KeychainSecretStoreTests.theLoginKeychainStoreReadsAnAddedItem` — `SecItemAdd gave status -25308` (errSecInteractionNotAllowed): the self-hosted runner's login keychain is locked. The user does not want to change the runner.
+
+## Do
+- [ ] `KeychainSecretStore` gets a keychain parameter (default: the login keychain, as today, so `KeychainSecretStore.loginKeychain(for:)`, RoutedACPAgent.swift:411 and SettingsStore.swift:255 keep their behaviour). Its query targets that keychain (e.g. `kSecUseKeychain` for add / `kSecMatchSearchList` for read, or whatever works for a file keychain).
+- [ ] The integration test creates a temporary keychain (unique file in a temp folder, known throwaway password, unlocked, no auto-lock), adds its item there, reads through a store given that keychain, and deletes the keychain file at the end — never touching the login keychain or the user's keychain search list.
+- [ ] Zero warnings: the file-keychain APIs (`SecKeychainCreate`, `SecKeychainOpen`, ...) are deprecated. Find a way with no build warning (e.g. the `security` CLI for create/unlock/delete in the test, and a non-deprecated way for the store to target it; or confine any deprecated call so it produces no warning). If no warning-free way exists, stop and report it.
+
+## Tests (first)
+- The integration test passes on a machine whose login keychain is locked (simulate: it must not use the login keychain at all).
+- A unit test: the store's queries carry the given keychain.
+- Run the IntegrationTests package locally (`cd IntegrationTests && swift test --filter KeychainSecretStoreTests`, with whatever gate env the CI workflow sets). #ci
\ No newline at end of file
